summary:
The main purpose of the Payment and Settlement (First Amendment) Bill, 2083 is to develop, expand, promote, monitor, and regulate the overall payment, clearing, and settlement system of the country, and to address practical complexities observed during the implementation of the Act (Statement of Objectives and Reasons, Page 1). This Act shall come into force immediately (Section 1, Subsection 2, Page 1).

Banks, financial institutions, or payment service provider institutions may appoint agents to perform payment service work (Section 5, Page 2). Institutions established abroad operating payment transactions internationally may submit an application with specified documents and fee to operate in Nepal (Section 6, Page 2). Institutions must maintain confidentiality of customer personal details (Section 20, Subsection 1, Page 3). When providing details to technology provider institutions during technology or system development and maintenance, institutions must provide them according to standards determined by the Bank (Section 20, Subsection 3, Page 3). Institutions must operate reliable and quality services ensuring consumer rights protection and payment security (Section 21, Page 3). Every institution and payment instrument issued by it must be connected to the national payment switch according to the procedure determined by the Bank (Section 16, Page 2). Every institution must compulsorily get its economic and financial position audited within four months of the end of every fiscal year (Section 18, Page 3). When submitting details, institutions must disclose their bank and e-money balance (Section 19, Page 3). Institutions must settle each payment order or transaction in real time or on a netted basis (Section 23, Subsections 1 and 2, Page 3). An institution whose license is revoked or not renewed must return the e-money amount to concerned customers within thirty days according to the procedure determined by the Bank (Section 27, Subsection 1, Page 4). If any dispute arises between institutions regarding payment transactions, such dispute must be resolved by mutual consent (Section 29, Subsection 1, Page 4).

An institution established abroad and operating internationally may submit an application for permission to the Bank with specified documents and fee, and site inspection shall not be required for such application (Section 6, Page 2; Section 7, Page 2). Permission may be refused if the nature of proposed transaction and business plan do not match the subject for which permission is requested (Section 8, Page 2). In the case of banks and financial institutions, opening a separate account for settlement of payment transactions shall not be required (Section 9, Page 2). The period of license shall be five years, but no period shall be specified for the license of banks and financial institutions, and for foreign institutions the Bank may determine a separate period and renewal procedure (Section 10, Subsections 1 and 6a, Page 2). The Bank may grant approval to expand services to institutions operating non-banking digital financial services or other digital platforms, and its approval and regulation shall be as determined by the Bank (Section 11, Subsections 1 and 2, Page 2). Institutions must apply as specified to add or cancel payment instruments or services (Section 12, Page 2). The Bank may invite applications regarding any new type of payment service and allow operation of service for testing, and its period, limit, and other arrangements shall be as determined by the Bank (Section 13, Subsections 1 and 2, Pages 2-3).

As a nominated expert member on the Board of Directors, the Government of Nepal shall nominate one member from among experts who have passed at least a Master's degree in economics, monetary, banking, finance, management, information technology, or commercial law and have at least five years of experience in the relevant field (Section 3, Subsection 1, Clause ch1, Pages 1-2). The tenure of the nominated member shall be two years, and the Government of Nepal may remove them if they fail to perform work (Section 3, Subsections 2 and 3, Page 2). The tenure of the chief executive shall be up to a maximum of four years and they may be reappointed once (Section 15, Subsection 4, Page 2). If disputes cannot be resolved by mutual consent, a Dispute Resolution Committee shall be formed under the chairmanship of the Executive Director overseeing the concerned department of the Bank, with Joint Secretary of the Ministry of Finance, Chief Executive Officer or head of concerned institution, and Head of Legal Division of the Bank as members, and Director of Payment Systems Department of the Bank as member-secretary (Section 29, Subsection 2, Page 4). Upon application, the committee shall resolve the dispute within fifteen days by summoning the other party and giving an opportunity of hearing, and that decision shall be final (Section 29, Subsections 3 and 4, Page 4). The Secretariat work of the committee shall be performed by the Payment Systems Department of the Bank (Section 29, Subsection 5, Page 4). Provisions regarding a fund are not stated in the bill (not stated in the bill).

The Bank may take action against a director or employee of an institution that violates the Act, regulations, directions, or orders or fails to provide details or documents requested by the Bank, the maximum fine for which is not stated in the bill (Section 25, Subsection 2, Page 3; not stated in the bill). Cases relating to offences specified in Section 36 shall have the Government of Nepal as plaintiff and shall be deemed to be included in Schedule-1 of the National Criminal Procedure Code, 2074 (Section 26, Page 3). The fine imposing authority, the right to appeal, its time limit, and the appeal court are not stated in the bill (not stated in the bill).
